description: A box cuts the spindle-torus head with a plane tilted 25 degrees from perpendicular to the axis. The pole becomes an interior point of the cut face. In each meridian, put k = tan(tilt) (cos(u) - sin(u))/sqrt(2). The cut y = 4 + k*r meets (r - 3)^2 + y^2 = 25 at the pole and at r_cut = (6 - 8*k)/(1 + k^2), where the wall's meridian angle is atan(4/3) + 2 atan(k). Area integrates the tilted disk, the flat base and the wall. For volume and moments integrate the primitive in y as a vertical flux, with r dr du on the tilted disk and -r dr du along the wall from 8 to r_cut. Over a turn atan(k) averages to zero and 1/(1 + k^2) averages to cos(tilt). Reflection in x = -z fixes the body. The inertia is evaluated by quadrature of the same flux.
